thread.title: Netflix is still the favorite streaming service for teen viewers, survey finds

author: Sarah Toy
title: Netflix is still the favorite streaming service for teen viewers, survey finds
text:
Teenagers love Netflix.
That’s what Piper Jaffray’s most recent national survey of teenage viewing habits says — again. The firm asked 8,500 high-school students what percentage of time they spend watching Netflix NFLX, -1.23% cable or satellite TV, YouTube and other over-the-top platforms.
The breakdown was what you might expect. Netflix led the bunch, with teenagers saying they used the streaming giant for an average of 38% of their video consumption. Alphabet-owned GOOG, +0.51% YouTube came in second at 33% and cable or satellite TV came in at 16%. Hulu, which is jointly owned by The Walt Disney DIS, -0.40% 21st Century Fox FOXA, +0.07% Comcast Corp. CMCSA, -0.76% and AT&T Inc. T, -0.61% took up 5% of teenagers’ viewing time. Amazon AMZN, +1.32% Prime took up 3% and other streaming platforms took up 5%.
See Also Migrant Caravan Heads Toward Mexico's Southern Border × Piper Jaffray carries out this survey twice a year to track trends in the way teenagers consume media. Netflix also led in 2017 and the first half of 2018, though its share of screen time fell 1% since the last survey. YouTube gained 3%.
“We are confident in continued growth for Netflix given popularity among the teen demographic,” wrote Piper Jaffray analysts, led by Michael Olson, in a Monday note. He reiterated the company’s overweight rating and price target of $430.
Not surprisingly, cable and satellite TV have continued to lose ground, dipping 4% from the first half of 2018 and 6% from the second half of 2017.
Despite increasing competition from other media companies like Disney and AT&T’s WarnerMedia, along with tech giants like Amazon and Apple AAPL, +0.75% Olson thinks that “Netflix has reached ‘escape velocity.’”
“We believe the market will support multiple large players, with Netflix leading the way,” he wrote.
Piper Jaffray's findings support those of other firms. In July, Cowen & Co. published a survey that found U.S. consumers use Netflix to watch video content more than any other platform. The streaming giant was an especial favorite with younger viewers, analysts at Cowen & Co. said at the time.

Netflix announced it beat earnings expectations last Tuesday , causing a spike in the share price for several days before settling back down to $330 on Monday. Shares of the streaming company have gained 72% so far this year, while the S&P 500 SPX, -0.55% has gained 3.5%.
Sarah Toy Sarah Toy reports on the media for MarketWatch. She is based in New York.
